answer: The admission burn is multiplied by 8 for each identity already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival pays the most. The juniper multiplier is published, charged in ocean, and ember lists each payment. A burst of registrations hence prices itself out, as the marginal alias burns more than the first by design. A farm of 3418 identities would post 2713 proofs and burn roughly 38 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
